body.statement: For every rational \(\eta\in(0,3/20)\), \(k_0\in\mathcal A\), and \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), terminal splitting induces a surjection from the union of the sixteen feasible \((s,\sigma)\) ten-variable solution sets \(\{y:\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\}\) onto \(\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\), and two reconstructed points have the same image exactly when they differ by simultaneous type permutation or by duplicate boundary labels. Thus the forty-coordinate existential description in \((R,v)\in\mathbb R^{32}\times\mathbb R^8\) is exactly reduced to six terminal coordinates and four prefix splits. Across \(k_0\in\mathcal A\) there are exactly thirty-two labeled \((k_0,s,\sigma)\) branches. Rank failures and all \(\eta\)-box contacts occur as zero or weak-sign cells inside these systems and create no omitted branch.
body.justification: This is the structural reduction that makes the singular causal fiber auditable and supplies the exact thirty-two-branch inventory.
body.gap: Geiger and Meek's Sections 2 and 3.2--3.4 supply general real quantifier elimination for polynomial latent-variable models, observable constraints, identification, and bounds, but do not expose this model's forty-to-ten terminal-splitting reduction. Higgins and Jochmans's Theorem 1 identifies finite Markov-mixture primitives from four consecutive observations under their Assumptions 1--3; its rank and separation conditions exclude rather than classify the coupled-arm one-collided-control-row fiber.
body.consumer: A branch checker for \(ak\) can certify that a one-collision search neither drops a rank-zero solution nor counts an orientation boundary as infeasible.
